_about: The seven role templates of the Hand-off Standard (HANDOFF-STANDARD.md, decision 19). One entry per role; handoff.py renders handoff.md from these. Roles, never names. `needs` are the inputs a hand-off for this role cannot leave without; `publish` marks the roles whose work goes live and therefore stop at rule 6 (nothing goes live without the owner's go).

creator-manager.title: Creator manager
creator-manager.inside: every creator-handoff ready to send; the brief-to-creator match by talent card and avatar fit; due dates; a status sheet
creator-manager.told: who gets what, what done looks like, what to chase
creator-manager.comes_back: sent and delivered status for every creator-handoff
creator-manager.stops_at: sending a brief to a creator
steps: Open briefs/ — one folder per brief, each with brief.md and brief.json.

For every brief pick the creator whose talent card fits the avatar named in brief.json (components/casting). Write the match to returned/matches.json: brief id, creator id (a role-side id, never a person's name), due date.
Build one creator-handoff folder per matched creator (this same skill: `handoff creator <brand> <brief ids>`), so every creator gets one folder of briefs.
Write returned/status.md: sent / delivered / chased per creator-handoff, one line each.
STOP before sending anything to a creator. Sending is the go.
returned: matches.json — brief id → creator id, due date
status.md — sent / delivered / chased per creator-handoff

creator.title: Creator (brief writer's package for one creator)
creator.inside: start-here; one brief per piece; inspiration and reference videos; the product's record in the catalog; the landing page by link id
creator.told: what to film or shoot; the rules (9:16, clean, no watermark); naming and how to return
creator.comes_back: raw footage and pictures named with brief and asset ids
creator.stops_at: nothing goes live; hands back only
steps: Read handoff.md, then briefs/<brief id>/brief.md for each piece.
Film or shoot exactly what each brief asks. 9:16, clean background unless the brief says otherwise, no watermark, no filter that changes skin.
Name every file `<brief id>_<asset id>.<ext>` (asset-01, asset-02, …) and put it in returned/.
Write returned/notes.md — one line per file: brief id, asset id, what it is.

clipper.title: Clipper
clipper.inside: open briefs with scenes and references; the product's record in the catalog; the page by link id; captions
clipper.told: the open briefs, the posting rules, what a finished clip is
steps: Read handoff.md and each briefs/<brief id>/brief.md.
Cut the clip or build the slideshow the brief describes; captions from references/captions when present.
Name every finished file `<brief id>_<asset id>.<ext>` and put it in returned/.
Write returned/posted.json: brief id, asset id, where it is to be posted, the link once it is live — leave the link empty until the owner's go.
STOP before posting. Posting is the go.
returned: posted.json — asset → platform, link (empty until go)

graphic-designer.title: Graphic designer
graphic-designer.comes_from: image, sequence, email and page briefs
graphic-designer.inside: static and sequence: the draft, the plate, product pictures, layout data, the exact words, the variations · email: the wireframe, the reference email, the copy, the picture jobs · page: the page copy, the picture map, the product's record in the catalog
graphic-designer.told: what to finish; what cannot change (product, words, offer, link); the sizes
graphic-designer.comes_back: finished files named to the standard
graphic-designer.stops_at: nothing goes live; hands back only
steps: Read handoff.md, then briefs/<brief id>/brief.md — the words, the layout and the variations are in the brief; assets/ lists what exists already.
Finish each piece with the tools named above. A change to a picture is one delta at a time (image-edit); never redraw the product, never retype the words.
Every finished file is named to the naming standard — the ad name from brief.json plus `_asset-NN`; a name that does not parse is not finished.
Put finished files in returned/ and write returned/index.json: file → brief id, asset id, what changed.
returned: <ad name>_asset-NN.png — finished statics or sequence frames
index.json — file → brief id, asset id, what changed

video-editor.title: Video editor
video-editor.inside: clips per scene, the voice, music and sound, the cut sheet, the caption look, the hook versions
video-editor.told: the scene order and timing, the locked parts, one 9:16 master inside the 4:5 safe area
video-editor.stops_at: nothing goes live; hands back only
tools: tools/video-edit (`machine/run.py handoff <this folder>` — stops at the timeline and the captions; `--approve timeline|captions` on the owner's word)
steps: First time on this computer: read START-HERE.md in the role folder (Shared Assets/handoffs/video-editor/START-HERE.md). Every time: claim the ad on the shared work queue before cutting (`tools/video-production/machine/work_queue.py claim <brief>`) — if another computer holds it, leave it.
Read handoff.md; the edit kit is under assets/kit (cut sheet, clips per scene, voice, music, caption look, hook versions).
Run the edit line on the kit (`run.py handoff <this folder>`). Locked parts (the words, the product shots, the offer bar) do not move.
Stop at the timeline, then at the captions: each goes on only on the owner's approval (`--approve timeline`, then `--approve captions`).
The master (one 9:16 per brief, content inside the 4:5 safe area) is named `<ad name>_asset-NN.mp4`, put in returned/, and take-back writes returned/index.json: file → brief id, asset id, version.
returned: <ad name>_asset-NN.mp4 — one master per brief plus hook versions
index.json — file → brief id, asset id, version

ad-uploader.title: Ad uploader
ad-uploader.inside: the named ads, the copy, the landing page by link id, the ad set plan, the import sheet
ad-uploader.told: the exact ad name (nothing appended), the landing page in the URL field, the checks
ad-uploader.comes_back: the Meta ad id per ad
tools: lab/meta-upload (`build.py --brand --lane --run --out` — builds the import sheet; every row PAUSED; talks to nothing)
steps: Read handoff.md; the pictures are in assets/ads/<short name>/, and assets/index.json lists every ad by its short name with its old name beside it, its pictures and its copy row; references/links.json carries the landing page by link id.
Build the import sheet with meta-upload `build.py` into returned/import/. Every row lands PAUSED.

Check: each ad goes up under its short-form Meta ad name from section 3 of handoff.md, exactly (nothing appended); an ad already live on Meta keeps its old name there; the URL field is the working URL for the link id in references/links.json; every picture the sheet names exists.
Write returned/live-ids.json with one entry per ad — `{"ad_name": …, "channel": "meta", "platform_id": null}` — the platform id stays null until the ad exists in Meta.
STOP. The import sheet is parked. Uploading it to Meta is the go.
returned: import/ — the Meta bulk-import sheet plus the pictures it names, every row PAUSED
live-ids.json — ad name → Meta ad id (null until it exists)

klaviyo-uploader.title: Klaviyo uploader
klaviyo-uploader.inside: the email and its pictures, the subject lines, the send date, the audience
klaviyo-uploader.told: which send, which audience, which subject; the checks
klaviyo-uploader.comes_back: the Klaviyo campaign id per send
tools: tools/email-production (`push_klaviyo.py <run> --brand --pick N` — creates a DRAFT campaign; has no send call)
steps: Read handoff.md; assets/email lists the run's final HTML, the numbered subject set and the picked pair; references/links.json carries every link by id.
Check every link in the HTML is one of the link ids in references/links.json, and that the offer words in the email match references/offer-record.json.
Create the campaign as a DRAFT with push_klaviyo.py (`--pick` the numbered pair named in handoff.md).
Write returned/live-ids.json — `{"send": <label>, "channel": "klaviyo", "platform_id": <campaign id>, "status": "DRAFT"}`.
STOP. The campaign stays a DRAFT. Scheduling or sending is the go.
returned: live-ids.json — send → Klaviyo campaign id, status DRAFT

needs_words.brief_file: the brief itself (brief.md) — from the brief's run folder or the brand's briefs folder
needs_words.product: the product's record in the catalog
needs_words.link: at least one landing page, by link id, in the catalog
needs_words.ads: the finished ads — a drop with one folder per ad
needs_words.copy: a copy row for every ad
